records.title: Corvex: Take ownership of a working equity and options trading platform
records.description:
Start with a functioning product. Build its next chapter.

Corvex is a trading workflow platform for active equity and options traders. It brings brokerage connectivity, portfolio visibility, and trade management into a focused interface designed to help users work through the trading day with less friction.

The technical foundation is built. I’m looking for an entrepreneurial student or small team interested in taking responsibility for product direction, customer discovery, and business development.

What the product does

Active traders often work across broker interfaces, market news, portfolio tools, and spreadsheets. Corvex is designed to bring those activities into a more coherent workspace:

  • Connect and manage a Schwab account, with connection diagnostics, reconnect controls, and status visibility.
  • Monitor portfolio value, profit and loss, sector allocation, and daily movers.
  • View market news alongside portfolio information.
  • Work through a structured interface for placing, monitoring, and managing trades.
  • Review positions and account activity with greater clarity.

The intended customers are active equity and options traders who value control, usability, and a disciplined workflow.

Who I’m looking for

Someone interested in financial technology, trading, product design, or entrepreneurship who wants to take ownership of an existing product.

The next stage is to identify the strongest customer segment, understand how those traders work, test the business model, and decide which capabilities deserve further investment. That could include customer interviews, product testing, pricing, distribution, and evaluating additional data or brokerage integrations.

Experience with trading or financial software would be useful. Technical skills would also help, but the central requirement is a willingness to understand customers, make decisions, and execute.

records.title: Arbiter: Take ownership of a working sports arbitrage platform
records.description:
Start with a functioning platform. Decide how to build the business.

Arbiter is a sports arbitrage platform that identifies pricing differences across sportsbooks and exchanges, calculates stake allocations, and supports the workflow from opportunity detection through settlement and reconciliation.

The software is built. I’m looking for an entrepreneurial student or small team interested in taking it forward: validating the customer need, setting product priorities, developing the business model, and bringing it to market.

What the product does

Finding an apparent arbitrage opportunity is only part of the problem. Odds move, balances sit across different platforms, account limits affect execution, and settlement rules can differ. Arbiter brings these operational tasks into one workspace:

  • Monitor odds and detect arbitrage opportunities across 20+ exchanges.
  • Normalize events and pricing across moneylines, spreads, totals, and props.
  • Calculate stake allocations with fees and per-outcome profit-and-loss scenarios.
  • Generate trade tickets and support execution decisions.
  • Track balances, capital movements, and expected settlement timing.
  • Reconcile expected and actual results.
  • Assess execution confidence and account limitation risk when sizing positions.

The intended customers are serious sports arbitrage operators and quantitative traders managing activity across multiple sportsbooks and exchanges. Apparent pricing opportunities do not guarantee realized profits; execution, fees, limits, and settlement differences matter.

Who I’m looking for

Someone interested in quantitative finance, trading systems, sports analytics, B2B software, or product management who wants to take responsibility for the business.

The next stage involves talking to potential customers, testing pricing and distribution, evaluating data-provider relationships, and deciding which capabilities matter most. Understanding the applicable operating requirements and platform terms would also be part of that work.

Technical or quantitative experience would be useful. Equally valuable is someone who can understand the customer, challenge assumptions, and turn a working product into something people will pay to use.

How this could work

Arbiter is available for acquisition. I’m also open to an equity partnership or a student taking on product and business development leadership. Responsibilities, ownership, compensation, and time commitment would be discussed and agreed upon together.

I can provide mentorship, technical guidance, and transition support, with the scope agreed up front. The opportunity is to take ownership of an existing product and its direction.

About the founder

I’m John Casano, founder of Strike Labs, a Connecticut-based software development and venture firm. My background includes quantitative finance, hedge fund risk, alternative-data products, and software development. I’ve also worked with Tsai CITY for several years as a mentor, judge, and facilitator of one-on-one and small-group workshops.

Arbiter began as a technical problem I wanted to solve. Building it reinforced that I’m more interested in creating trading systems than running a sports betting business. I’d like to find someone who wants to develop the customer relationships and business around the software.

Interested?

records.title: Build an AI tool that takes the pulse of democracy
records.description:
Democracy is a conversation, yet no one can say with data how healthy that conversation is, whether it is getting better, or whether it is healthier in Mexico or Malaysia. The Public Sphere Index sets out to answer that.

Developed at Yale Law School’s Information Society Project and tested in an EU-funded pilot with human researchers, the Index first identifies the media that most shape a country’s conversation, weighted by reach, relevance, and the quality of their arguments. It then scores that core against seven determinants of a healthy public sphere, from truth and civility to pluralism and efficacy. The idea recently completed NSF's iCorps with Yale Ventures, receiving positive feedback from governments and international organizations around the world. A second pilot is currently underway and funded by the Federal Foreign Office of Germany. 

Your job is to build the prototype of the automated index. 

What you’ll do

  • Build the pipeline that ingests a country’s news through GDELT and other sources
  • Design a compelling experience and dashboard for users
  • Test LLM scoring for qualitative ideals like Civility
  • Track the results across countries and over time

The open research question is whether AI can judge these ideals as reliably as trained people can. This is a volunteer research role, with an opportunity to be a co-author on the resulting paper. Hours are flexible, and we’ll scope the work together.

You’ll work directly with me, Belabbès Benkredda, Entrepreneur in Residence at the Jackson School.

records.title: Yale INSPIRE: Ananth Sriskandarajah, Founder and CEO of Greenweaver AI
records.description:
Yale INSPIRE is a speaker series that brings visionary founders, innovators, and changemakers to campus for candid conversations about the moments that shaped their journeys. Go beyond the headlines to hear about the lessons, setbacks, breakthroughs, and bold decisions behind building what’s next.

In partnership with the Yale AI Association, join us for a fireside chat with Ananth Sriskandarajah, Founder and CEO of Greenweaver AI, exploring what it takes to build at the intersection of AI, climate, and infrastructure.

Greenweaver AI is building sovereign, low-carbon AI infrastructure through modular micro data centers that combine high-performance computing with heat reuse. Ananth’s work focuses on the intersection of AI, climate, infrastructure, and institutional capital.

Previously, Ananth served as Managing Director and Head of Ventures at Round Hill Capital, where he launched and led its venture strategy, invested across Europe, and served on the Investment Committee and Executive Committee. Earlier in his career, he held leadership roles at HelloFresh, Bloomsbury AI, and The Collective, and worked across strategy and investment at Capital & Counties PLC. He also served as an Entrepreneur in Residence at the European Commission supporting StartupEurope.

Ananth is also the Founder of Ground Floor Ventures, an angel syndicate backing ambitious early-stage founders. He has been recognized in WIRED 100 and Forbes 30 Under 30.

Whether you’re building your first startup, curious about the future of AI, or interested in how technology, climate, and capital intersect, come hear directly from a leader working across these rapidly evolving fields.

A networking reception with light bites will follow the talk.

records.description:

PatternQuest is a story-driven mobile game (iOS and Android) for self-guided wellness. Players explore a world where recurring life patterns become realms and characters, guided by an AI companion. Along the way they learn to spot the thinking habits that keep them stuck and turn what they learn into real-world change.

Our goal is to make self-understanding feel like an adventure, not a chore. Most wellness apps lose nearly all their users within a month. We're building one people want to come back to.

Real ownership of an early-stage venture and a portfolio project at the intersection of AI, mental health, and games.

records.title: Afore Capital Founders-in-Residence (FIR)
records.description: Rolling, year-round pre-idea and pre-seed program investing at least $100K into roughly 10 teams per cohort over two months in South Park, San Francisco. Distinct from Afore's FIR University track — the main FIR program has no school or enrollment requirement. Cohort kickoffs are Oct 1, 2026 (Fall) and Feb 1, 2027 (Spring). FLAGS: dilutive; conflicting cohort banners on the official page and no dated application deadline — confirm the current kickoff before applying.
records.ideal_candidate: Founder between things with strong technical or domain credentials who wants conviction capital before having a company.

records.title: GitHub Secure Open Source Fund
records.description: $10,000 per project paid in tranches, plus up to $150,000 in Azure credits, a three-week security program and GitHub Security Lab office hours. No equity is taken and no company is required — the grant goes to maintainers of existing open-source projects. Applicants must be 18+ and a maintainer (or team of at most two) on a project with real adoption. FLAGS: requires an already-adopted project, so this is not an idea-stage program. Applications are considered for all sessions on a rolling basis. Distinct from the GitHub Student Developer Pack.
records.company: GitHub (with Microsoft, Alfred P. Sloan Foundation, American Express)
records.ideal_candidate: Student maintainer of a widely depended-on open-source package who wants funding plus a real security review.

records.title: Amber Grant / Start-Up Grant
records.description: Three $10,000 grants awarded every month — one of them reserved for idea-stage and pre-revenue businesses via the Start-Up track — plus three $50,000 year-end grants drawn from the monthly winners. No equity, no repayment, and one application covers all eligible categories. Monthly cutoff is the last day of each month. FLAGS: GENDER-RESTRICTED — business must be at least 50% women-owned and the applicant 18+; US/Canada only; there is a $15 non-refundable application fee (waivable on request).
records.ideal_candidate: Woman student founder in the US or Canada, including pre-revenue and idea-stage ventures.

records.title: Northwestern Mutual Accelerator 2027
records.description: A corporate-backed accelerator that invests $100,000 directly into the startup's current round, or as an uncapped convertible bridge note if not raising. Focused on fintech, insurtech, digital health and data analytics. Open to startups globally provided at least one founder is based in the United States. Applications close October 30, 2026; program kicks off January 13, 2027.
records.ideal_candidate: Fintech, insurtech, digital health or data-analytics founders from any school, with at least one US-based founder.

records.title: 2026 $100,000 Start an SUD Startup Challenge
records.description: Up to $100,000 in non-dilutive prizes, with up to 12 teams receiving six months of NIDA mentorship and up to $10,000 each. Unusually founder-friendly: no incorporation required and no prior startup experience required. Teams of 3-5; the team leader must be a US citizen or lawful permanent resident. Topic must relate to drug use or substance use disorder. Excludes teams with existing SBIR/STTR applications. Closes 5:00 PM ET on November 2, 2026.
records.ideal_candidate: Student teams from any school with an idea addressing substance use disorder — no company, funding or prior startup experience needed.

records.title: One-Step, Rapid, Low-Cost Definitive Drug Testing at the Point of Need Challenge
records.description: Up to $600,000 in non-dilutive prize funding for point-of-need drug testing technology. Open to individuals or entities, so students can enter without a company. Phase 1 submissions open September 15, 2026 and close 5:00 PM ET on December 15, 2026. Requires a working prototype with proof-of-concept data — not an idea-stage challenge.
records.company: National Institutes of Health / NIDA with NIST
records.ideal_candidate: Student researchers and hardware founders from any school with a working diagnostic or sensing prototype.

records.title: Carnegie Challenge for Civic Leadership
records.description: A tiered civic-innovation challenge: $100 seed grants to up to 600 early applicants, then twelve $500 awards, ten $1,000 awards and two $10,000 awards, plus a travel-covered convening in July 2027. Early deadline November 17, 2026 (required for the $100 seed grant); final deadline January 30, 2027. FLAG: hard age cap — applicants must be 20 or younger as of January 31, 2027, so this only reaches freshmen, sophomores and some juniors.
records.company: Ashoka Changemakers + Carnegie Corporation of New York
records.ideal_candidate: College students aged 20 or under from any school working on civic engagement, democracy or community leadership ventures.

records.title: Runway Startup Postdoc Program
records.description: A two-year deep-tech postdoc that pays $175,000 in year one and $150,000 in year two, covering salary, research budget, housing allowance and space. The institute takes roughly 8.5% equity and the founder keeps a royalty-free perpetual IP license. Open to PhDs from ANY university — no Cornell or Technion affiliation required. Applications open October 15, 2026 and close February 1, 2027.
records.company: Jacobs Technion-Cornell Institute at Cornell Tech
records.ideal_candidate: PhD holders (graduated within 5 years or nearing completion) from any university who want to commercialize their research in New York. International applicants supported via J-1/O-1.

records.title: Entrepreneurship World Cup (current cycle)
records.description: Over $1,000,000 in 100% equity-free cash prizes across Idea, Early and Growth stages plus four $50,000 AI sub-track prizes. The Idea track requires no legal entity and no revenue, so solo student founders and student teams can enter. There is no application fee at any stage. Registration runs on a rolling basis through May 31, 2027. Note: the site's cycle labelling is inconsistent ('EWC 2026' branding alongside 2027 milestone dates) — the May 31, 2027 date comes from the dated official announcement.
records.location: Global — finals in Riyadh; open to US applicants
records.ideal_candidate: Any student founder 18 or over with a validated concept — no company, revenue or incorporation required for the Idea track.

records.title: BASE — Ballard Academy for Student Entrepreneurs
records.description: A nine-month pro bono virtual startup accelerator built specifically for student founders at any school, combining free legal work with programming and a closing pitch competition. FLAG: the structured 2026-2027 cohort application is closed; the firm has an open rolling intake by email for student founders and early-stage startups needing legal help. Delivered entirely pro bono.
records.ideal_candidate: Student founders at any university with a pre-seed to Series A venture needing startup legal counsel.

records.title: The Pollination Project Seed Grants
records.description: Non-dilutive seed grants of up to $500 awarded on a rolling basis by a network of 100+ volunteer grant advisors. Small but genuinely open — no incorporation required. Constraints: the organization's budget must be under $50,000, the project cost under $10,000, and the venture must have no paid staff.
records.ideal_candidate: Student founders from any school running a very early social-impact project that needs a first small unlock.

records.title: Elemental Impact — Project Track, Strategy Track & Data Center Innovation Initiative
records.description: A climate-focused nonprofit investor accepting rolling applications across three tracks, funding pre-seed through Series C. Reported up to roughly $3M per company, with the Data Center Innovation Initiative deploying $500K-$5M per project into up to 10 startups through 2027. Instruments include equity and the D-SAFE — this is dilutive investment, not a grant. Sectors: energy, industry, built environment, food and ag, nature, water, transportation.
records.location: Honolulu HI, New York NY, Washington DC, San Francisco CA
records.ideal_candidate: Climate and energy founders from any school with a company far enough along to take institutional investment.

records.title: The Forum Accelerator
records.description: A 16-week B2B SaaS pre-seed accelerator investing $100,000 for 7.5% on a standard post-money SAFE, plus $100,000+ in perks and a dedicated managing director. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with no cohort cutoff. Open to founders from any school; 26% of the last cohort were solo founders and 58% first-time founders.
records.location: New York, NY / San Francisco, CA / Toronto
records.ideal_candidate: First-time or solo B2B software founders, pre-seed, with under $500K raised and an MVP in market or close to it.

records.title: South Park Commons — Founder Fellowship & Member Residency
records.description: Two tracks for pre-idea and pre-company founders. The Founder Fellowship provides $1M total ($400K for 7% on a SAFE plus $600K guaranteed in the next round) and up to $1M in credits, running as spring and fall cohorts. The Member Residency is six months with no fee and no equity. Applications are accepted year-round on a rolling basis; the Fall 2026 fellowship cutoff has passed and Spring 2027 is expected around December.
records.location: San Francisco, CA and New York, NY
records.ideal_candidate: Students, PhDs and academics willing to leave or take a sabbatical from school to explore a company from scratch — SPC explicitly accepts undergrads through professors. Must work from the SF or NYC office.

records.title: HAX — SOSV Hard Tech Program
records.description: SOSV's hard tech program, distinct from the SOSV SF/NY application. Invests $550,000 at pre-seed with follow-on through seed, plus lab and prototyping infrastructure at Newark and the HAX Plasma Forge in Princeton. Runs a dedicated university track for student and researcher founders. Rolling applications; relocation to New Jersey required.
records.ideal_candidate: Hard tech, robotics, climate or industrial founders — including graduate students and researchers from any school — willing to relocate to New Jersey.

records.title: TigerLaunch 2027
records.description: Bills itself as the world's largest student entrepreneurship competition. Grand prize is $60,000 with no strings attached — fully non-dilutive, no equity taken — plus regional prizes, mentorship, and access to an alumni network of founders and investors. Applications opened September 1, 2026 and close October 25, 2026; regional competitions begin January 1, 2027 and finals are held at Princeton in April 2027.
records.location: Global — regional competitions worldwide, finals at Princeton, NJ
records.ideal_candidate: Student founders at any school with a startup idea and team, willing to pitch at a regional competition

records.title: The Founders Grant Program — $25,000 in Pro Bono Legal Services
records.description: One startup is selected in the first month of each calendar quarter to receive a $25,000 initial grant of pro bono legal services spanning corporate governance, IP, employment, and tax, plus an ongoing reduced-fee relationship and vendor and partner introductions. No equity is taken and there is no application fee. FLAG: explicitly targets founders from underrepresented backgrounds (BILPOC, first-generation, immigrant, formerly incarcerated, or differently-abled), and only one startup is selected per quarter — next selection is expected around October 2026.
records.ideal_candidate: Underrepresented founders at a growth inflection point who need substantive legal support they cannot yet pay for

records.title: NASA TechLeap Prize: Orbital Clarity Challenge (Challenge #6)
records.description: The awaited sixth NASA TechLeap challenge, opened 2026-08-19, seeking low-cost scalable methods to measure density, pressure, or drag in low Earth orbit for better satellite trajectory prediction. $2,000,000 total pool with up to four winners at up to $500,000 each across three phases, plus a free orbital flight test; prize money with no equity taken. No school affiliation required — students may enter as individuals or teams. FLAG: mandatory registration by 2026-10-28; individuals must be US citizens or permanent residents 18+; selected winners must demonstrate $250,000 in liability insurance coverage.
records.company: NASA Heliophysics Division + Flight Opportunities (administered by Luminary Labs)
records.ideal_candidate: Student aerospace, physics, or instrumentation teams with a novel sensing approach and the technical depth to survive a three-phase NASA review.

records.title: Techstars Spring 2027 Accelerators (US + Anywhere programs)
records.description: Techstars opened its Spring 2027 cycle on 2026-08-24 across its US programs — Anywhere (remote-first, no relocation), Boston, NYC (founders may be based anywhere), Chicago, Baltimore AI Health, and Northwestern Medicine Healthcare (only 6 startups). One application at apply.techstars.com covers all programs. Current terms are $220,000: a $20,000 post-money Convertible Equity Agreement for 5% common stock plus a $200,000 uncapped MFN SAFE. Program runs Mar 8 – Jun 3, 2027 with demo day Jun 3. Open to any early-stage founder worldwide with no school or age restriction; student founders eligible. FLAG: equity-taking, and most programs expect a full-time commitment.
records.location: Remote / Boston, MA / New York, NY / Chicago, IL / Baltimore, MD
records.ideal_candidate: Early-stage student founders with a working product or strong technical team, willing to commit full-time and take dilution for $220K plus a top-tier mentor network.

records.title: Federal SBIR/STTR Open Topics (All Agencies)
records.description: The federal SBIR/STTR portal currently lists 337 open topics across DoW/Army/Air Force/DARPA, NIH, DOE, NASA, USDA, DHS, and NIST, offering non-dilutive Phase I awards typically between $50,000 and $500,000 with no equity taken. Department of War releases open the first Wednesday of each month and close the last Wednesday of the following month, giving a predictable rolling entry point. Requires a US small business more than 50% owned by US citizens or permanent residents — students routinely incorporate to apply. No fee. Complements the NSF SBIR/STTR Project Pitch already on the board by covering every other agency.
records.company: US Small Business Administration / participating federal agencies
records.ideal_candidate: Student deep-tech founders with a technical co-founder, willing to incorporate and write a serious technical proposal for six-figure non-dilutive funding.

records.title: LG NOVA Mission for the Future — Innovation Program
records.description: Up to $100,000 in non-dilutive grant funding for pilots, proofs of concept, and joint product development, plus an entrepreneur-in-residence and LG global business development support. Any subsequent investment through the NOVA Prime Fund is separate and optional, so the grant itself is non-dilutive. Tracks are HealthTech, CleanTech, and Transformational Tech with a US market focus. Notably, published eligibility explicitly names individuals, academic researchers, entrepreneurs, and inventors as well as companies of any size — one of very few corporate programs that does not require an incorporated funded company. Applicant must be 18+ and a legal resident of a non-excluded country; no fee. FLAG: the submit page embeds a JavaScript form that could not be rendered during verification — confirm it loads before investing time.
records.company: LG Electronics North America Innovation Center
records.ideal_candidate: Student researchers and founders in health, clean, or frontier tech who want non-dilutive pilot funding and a corporate design partner.

records.title: Verizon Small Business Digital Ready — $10,000 National Grant
records.description: A $10,000 equity-free cash grant plus free courses, coaching, and events. Applications are reviewed monthly from June through December 2026 with roughly 10 businesses selected each month and all applicants receiving a final decision by 2027-01-12; apply once and you stay in the pool for every subsequent monthly cycle that year. Open to owners of for-profit small businesses based in the US, Puerto Rico, or USVI aged 18+, with no school, revenue, or state restriction and no fee. FLAG: you must register and complete any two free courses or events to unlock the application, and you need a registered for-profit entity.
records.ideal_candidate: Student founders who have already incorporated a for-profit entity and want straightforward non-dilutive cash with a low application bar.

records.title: gener8tor Madison Accelerator 2026
records.description: gener8tor Wisconsin's flagship Madison cohort invests $100,000 for 7.5% equity via SAFE in six startups per cohort, explicitly industry-agnostic and business-model-agnostic with no student restriction. Applications are live now on a rolling basis though cohort start dates have not yet been announced. FLAG: equity-taking; a Madison residency requirement could not be confirmed.
records.ideal_candidate: Student and early-stage founders in any vertical who want $100K and a concierge accelerator with no industry filter.

records.title: gener8tor Bronze Valley Investment Accelerator Delaware 2027
records.description: Twelve-week concierge program investing $100,000 for 5% equity via SAFE — the cheapest equity price of any currently open gener8tor cohort. Up to five startups selected regardless of industry or business model, with no student restriction. Rolling applications with no posted close date. FLAG: equity-taking and Delaware-anchored.
records.ideal_candidate: Early-stage founders, including students, who want $100K on relatively founder-friendly terms and can be based in or travel to Delaware.

records.title: Curql Accelerate — Spring 2027
records.description: Twelve-week blended virtual and in-person accelerator running January 14 – April 23, 2027 for B2B fintech startups serving credit unions, with a $7,000 non-dilutive grant to cover participation and travel costs — no equity is taken. Only five companies are selected per cohort, giving direct access to credit union executives and Curql's limited partners. FLAGS: narrow vertical (credit-union fintech only); requires travel to three week-long US on-sites.
records.location: Global; hybrid with three week-long credit union on-sites in the US
records.ideal_candidate: Student founders from any school, anywhere in the world, building B2B fintech products that credit unions would buy.

records.title: PMF Method — Fall 2026
records.description: Free four-day intensive run by First Round Capital partners on customer discovery and the path to product-market fit, held September 27–30, 2026. Completely free with no equity taken and no investment made — it is a workshop, not a funding program. Applications are open on a rolling basis with selections notified by September 4, 2026. FLAGS: must attend in person in Sonoma, CA; no funding attached; focused on B2B SaaS and AI-native B2B.
records.ideal_candidate: Early-stage founders building a new B2B SaaS or AI-native B2B company who have raised under $2M; pre-idea and pre-company founders are explicitly welcome, and there is no school restriction.

records.title: Founder University — Cohort 13
records.description: Twelve-week virtual pre-accelerator requiring roughly 5–10 hours per week plus two one-hour live sessions, with $25,000 invested into top graduates and a separate LAUNCH Accelerator track offering $125,000 for 7%. The Cohort 13 application portal is live and accepting submissions on a rolling basis with no published deadline. FLAGS: date conflict — the homepage advertises 'Cohort 13 — Fall 2026' while the live application portal's cohort dropdown offers 'Cohort 13 - Early 2027'; confirm the start date before committing. Open to any tech startup founder with no school restriction.
records.ideal_candidate: Student founders from any school who want structured startup training at a part-time commitment level compatible with being enrolled.

records.title: eMerge Global Startup Accelerator + Showcase 2027
records.description: Six weeks of virtual training, 1:1 mentorship, a Founders' Day, an expo booth, and a main-stage pitch at the eMerge Americas conference March 2–4, 2027, competing for over $300,000 in investment funding plus in-kind legal services, with no equity taken. The Pre-Seed track requires only an MVP with little or no revenue — no full-time-employee or revenue minimum. Sectors: National Security, AI and Deep Tech, Health, and Finance. FLAGS: a $650 participation fee is charged only if you are selected (this is a program fee, not an entry fee — applying is free); the Seed and Series A tracks do require 2 full-time employees plus revenue, but Pre-Seed does not; cohort is capped at 100 companies and no close date is published, so apply early.
records.ideal_candidate: Student founders from any school with a working prototype in national security, AI, deep tech, health, or fintech who can travel to Miami Beach in March 2027.

records.title: Geoffrey H. Palmer Startup Law Clinic — Free Legal Services
records.description: Free startup legal services supervised by startup attorney Prof. Sam Wu (formerly of Wilson Sonsini) — clients pay only government filing fees and no equity is taken. The clinic has incorporated roughly 50 startups over six years, handling Delaware formation, cap tables, founder stock with vesting, bylaws, user agreements, corporate governance, and angel and VC financings; several clients went on to raise venture capital and enter Silicon Valley accelerators. Open to outside founders at any school or none. FLAGS: practically Los Angeles / California-centric; excludes patent prosecution, tax, and regulatory work (handled by referral instead); clients are vetted for fit and the page currently reads 'Accepting New Client Applications'.
records.company: Pepperdine Caruso School of Law (Palmer Center for Entrepreneurship and the Law)
records.ideal_candidate: Student founders from any school with an early-stage startup that has not yet closed a significant financing round and needs formation, equity, and governance work done properly.

records.title: Entrepreneurship & Community Development Clinic — Client Intake
records.description: Free transactional legal services covering entity choice and formation, employment law, trademark and copyright registration, contract and lease drafting and negotiation, tax-exemption applications, and regulatory and licensing work — clients cover only government filing fees and no equity is taken. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and the clinic explicitly takes the bulk of its clients during August and January, so intake is at its peak right now. Open to outside founders from any school. FLAGS: region-restricted — must be located in New York State, preferably the five boroughs; means-tested for low-to-moderate income founders who cannot afford outside counsel and have no significant outside investor funding; must serve a community need and have a detailed business plan; excludes litigation, patents, complex tax, securities, and M&A; requires an in-person interview and a signed retainer.
records.ideal_candidate: New York-based student founders from any school building community-serving ventures who cannot afford counsel and have not raised significant outside investment.

records.title: LvlUp Ventures — One Application to 25+ VC Funds
records.description: Single rolling funding application reviewed by LvlUp Ventures (ranked #4 most active VC firm in the US and #7 globally by Pitchbook) and routed to 25+ alliance venture partners including Insight Partners and Greycroft. Covers multiple funds: industry-agnostic seed, CPG, First Check Fund (1,000 investments planned in 2026), and several non-dilutive financing funds for B2B SaaS, tech, CPG, and brick-and-mortar businesses. Free to apply; open to the general public including student founders; investment/financing terms vary by fund. Flag: LvlUp's separate Labs/bootcamp programs may carry fees — this entry is for the free funding application only.
records.ideal_candidate: Pre-seed to growth-stage founder (student founders welcome) in tech, CPG, e-commerce, B2B SaaS, or real-economy businesses seeking equity investment or non-dilutive financing with a single application.

records.title: Hypothesis-to-Evidence Grant
records.description: Fully-funded pilot covering up to $5,000 of wet-lab execution (paid directly to the lab vendor) to test one computational prediction — e.g., SPR/BLI binding, IC50 enzyme inhibition, DNA synthesis, LNP characterization, LC-MS — plus 2 months of K-Dense Web Plus (~$400 value), vendor sourcing, and ~2-3 week turnaround; 3 awards per cycle. Open to researchers at any career stage from any school: PhD candidates, postdocs, faculty, biotech founders and early-stage R&D teams (undergrads/independent researchers case-by-case). Flags: not a cash stipend — funds go straight to the lab; requires a public case study and program citation in any resulting publications (partly a marketing program for K-Dense/Litmus); costs beyond $5K are the fellow's responsibility.
records.location: Remote / global (experiments via vetted US lab network)
records.ideal_candidate: Student researcher or biotech/deeptech founder with a specific, testable hypothesis from a computational lead that can be settled by one scoped wet-lab experiment within $5K and 2-3 weeks.

records.title: Lawyers for a Sustainable Economy — Free Legal Services for Sustainability Startups
records.description: Pro bono legal services program: 21 major firms (Wilson Sonsini, Cooley, Orrick, Latham, Fenwick, Perkins Coie, etc.) have pledged ~$27M in free legal work for sustainability-focused startups and nonprofits — formation, contracts, IP, financing, tax, privacy. No equity, no fees, rolling intake; no school affiliation needed. Flags: environmental-sustainability focus only; firm matching not guaranteed.
records.company: Stanford Law School ENRLP + 21 major law firms
records.ideal_candidate: Student founders (any school) building climate/sustainability startups that need incorporation, IP, or financing legal work

records.title: Claude for Startups — Free API Credits & Priority Rate Limits
records.description: Anthropic's startup program: free Claude API credits and an upgrade to the highest-tier rate limits, plus hackathons, Founder Days, meetups in six cities, and early access to model releases. Credits require equity funding from an institutional investor, founding within the last 4 years, and no prior Anthropic startup credits (mention an Anthropic partner VC/accelerator for extra benefits); the community program is open to any early-stage founder, including students. FLAGS: credits work only on the first-party Claude API (not Bedrock/Vertex); credit dollar amounts are not published officially.
records.ideal_candidate: Student founders building AI products on the Claude API — VC-backed founders qualify for credits; any early-stage founder can join for community and early access

records.title: SXSW Pitch 2027 — Student Startups Category
records.description: SXSW's flagship startup competition has a dedicated Student Startups category (the presenting founder must be actively enrolled at event time); other tracks cover fintech, health, sustainability/agtech, and frontier tech. No guaranteed cash prize — the value is pitching live to VCs and press (80%+ of alumni have raised funding); no equity taken. FLAGS: non-refundable application fee ($105 early bird by 2026-09-13, $225 through the final 2026-11-13 deadline); product must have launched after Jan 1, 2024 with under $10M raised.
records.ideal_candidate: An enrolled student founder with a launched product and traction who can budget the fee and Austin travel.

records.title: Startup Legal Garage — Fall 2026 Cohort
records.description: A semester of free startup legal work (incorporation, contracts, IP, or patents) performed by UC Law SF student attorneys supervised by senior startup/VC law firm lawyers — $25M+ in legal services delivered to 550+ startups to date, with no fees and no equity. Open to the general public including student founders; best fit is pre-Series A companies under $1M in funding/revenue with an MVP and discrete legal needs. Fall 2026 (Aug–Nov) applications are open now and close when the cohort fills — apply early.
records.company: UC Law San Francisco (Center for Innovation)
records.ideal_candidate: A student founder with an MVP who needs incorporation, contracts, or patent groundwork done free before fundraising.

records.title: Draper Richards Kaplan Foundation Funding
records.description: Up to $300,000 of unrestricted funding over 3 years for early-stage social enterprises (nonprofit or for-profit), with a DRK partner joining your board. Applications are accepted year-round and take 30–60 minutes; extremely selective (~20 of 2,200+ applicants a year) and requires evidence of a working pilot, not just an idea. Open to the general public including student founders, globally.
records.ideal_candidate: A student-founded social enterprise with demonstrated pilot impact and a credible plan to scale.

records.title: NVIDIA Inception — free AI startup program with GPU training & partner credits
records.description: Free rolling membership program for AI/tech startups: DLI training credits, preferred hardware/software pricing, partner cloud credits (up to $100K AWS Activate, up to $150K Nebius via partners), and the Inception Capital Connect VC network — no fees, no equity, no cohorts or deadlines. Open to the general public including student-founded startups. Note: must be incorporated (<10 years old) with at least one developer and a working website; consultancies and crypto excluded.

records.title: Telora Fellowship (January 2027 cohort)
records.description: 6-month funded fellowship explicitly built as a student-to-founder pipeline: $10,000 initial deposit, hands-on startup help, no idea/MVP/cofounder required, ~1-minute application. Unusual terms: no conventional equity — founders pay 10% of personal proceeds only if they make $4M+ from a sale; otherwise nothing. FLAGS: full-time 6 months (no school or jobs); Miami relocation; most fellows under 24; US/Canada work authorization required, no visa sponsorship; June and January cohorts, apply up to a year ahead.
records.ideal_candidate: An under-24 student hacker willing to take a semester+ off and go all-in in Miami.

records.title: HF0 Residency
records.description: 12-week live-in residency where founder teams build from an SF mansion with housing and meals handled; rolling applications, multiple cohorts per year. Reported terms (third-party; not published on official site): up to $1M on an uncapped SAFE for 5% equity. Open to the general public — students accepted but the bar skews toward strong technical founders. FLAGS: 5% equity; full-time; 12-week SF relocation; confirm terms with HF0.
records.ideal_candidate: An intensely focused technical founding team ready to sprint full-time toward a launch.

records.title: Entrepreneurs First - US Funding & Fellowships
records.description: The 'talent investor' funds individuals pre-idea and pre-team: 3-month SF residencies to experiment, find a cofounder, and build, with EF historically investing ~$250K (equity) and follow-on potential. Rolling applications for US-based individuals; no cofounder or idea needed — students and new grads are a core audience. FLAGS: equity on investment; full-time; in-person SF; separate Bridge/London tracks are Europe-only.
records.ideal_candidate: A high-achieving student or early-career builder without a cofounder who wants a structured path to founding.

records.title: Founders, Inc. (f.inc)
records.description: Founder campus plus early-stage fund: rolling general application feeds first checks (typically ~$50K-$250K, equity) and program cohorts (AI x Hardware residency, off-season grants), with desk/lab space and weekly demo days at a 42,000 sq ft Fort Mason campus. Open to the public with no credential requirements — young and student builders are a large share of the community. FLAGS: equity on investment; in-person SF culture.
records.ideal_candidate: A scrappy student builder who wants SF community and a small first check before institutional rounds.

records.title: Alchemist Accelerator (Flagship)
records.description: The top enterprise/B2B-focused seed accelerator: 6-month program, 7K+ mentors, investor demo day; applications accepted any time and reviewed at the next application date (Alchemist Chicago sub-program window: Jul 13-Aug 20, 2026). Historically ~$25K for ~5% equity (not stated on current page — confirm). Open to the public; student teams eligible with a real company. FLAGS: equity; enterprise/B2B focus.
records.ideal_candidate: A technical student team selling to enterprises that wants structured GTM and fundraising prep.

records.title: Boost VC (Pre-Seed + $50K Fellowship)
records.description: Adam Draper's frontier-tech fund with an always-open application: $500K pre-seed lead/co-lead checks ($100K-$1M flexible) plus a dedicated $50K Fellowship track for founders too early to raise a full pre-seed; free founder housing at Draper University when visiting. Open globally to the public, students included. FLAGS: equity (terms per deal); frontier/'sci-fi' thesis (robotics, bio, space, crypto, energy — not pure SaaS); no cohort structure.
records.ideal_candidate: A very early deep-tech student founder who needs a first $50K and a believer, not a program.

records.title: Frontier Residency (Batch 1)
records.description: 8-week SF 'landing pad' residency for 10 teams starting October 2026: accommodation, workspace in the 16-floor Frontier Tower (750+ builders), lunches, and a demo day with 250+ investors — for 3% equity. Applications open now with rolling review; open to the public including student founders. FLAGS: 3% equity; full-time 8-week SF relocation.
records.ideal_candidate: An out-of-town early founder who wants a low-friction first two months in San Francisco.

records.title: 500 Global Flagship Accelerator (Batch 37)
records.description: 500 Global's flagship accelerator (est. 2010) invests in early-stage tech startups across regions and industries, hosted at its Palo Alto HQ; the official portal confirms Batch 37 applications are open now. Reported terms (third-party; confirm with 500): $150,000 for 6% equity with a $37,500 program fee deducted from the investment. Open to the general public and accepts student founders. FLAGS: equity taken + program fee; in-person Palo Alto program; portal's 'Batch 37 starts Q2 2026' text appears stale.
records.ideal_candidate: A student team with a launched product and early traction ready to relocate to Palo Alto for an in-person batch.

records.title: Y Combinator (late Fall 2026 applications + Early Decision for students)
records.description: The flagship accelerator's $500K standard deal ($125K for 7% + $375K uncapped MFN SAFE). Fall 2026 on-time deadline passed July 27 but the official page confirms late applications are still accepted, and Early Decision lets currently enrolled students at any school apply now for 2027 batches with funding secured on acceptance. FLAGS: 7%+ equity; full-time commitment and SF relocation for the batch; late applicants get no guaranteed review timeline.
records.ideal_candidate: An ambitious student team (any vertical, especially AI) willing to commit full-time, now or after graduation via Early Decision.

records.title: Cloudflare for Startups — $10K in credits for bootstrapped founders
records.description: Credits for Cloudflare compute, Workers AI, storage, and delivery. The base $10K tier is explicitly for bootstrapped or self-funded startups with under $1M raised — no minimum funding required. Higher tiers reach $350K.

records.title: DigitalOcean Startups — cloud & GPU credits, no accelerator needed
records.description: Cloud and AI/GPU credits for early-stage startups that have raised $10M or less. Apply directly — no accelerator or VC affiliation required (select 'Other' for affiliation).

records.title: MongoDB for Startups — free Atlas credits, bootstrapped welcome
records.description: Free MongoDB Atlas credits plus Voyage AI embedding tokens and one-on-one technical advice. Open to startups under 7 years old at Series A or earlier — founders without a VC or accelerator apply directly on the page.

records.title: ElevenLabs Startup Grants — 33M characters of free AI audio
records.description: 33 million characters of free voice and audio generation over 12 months (680+ hours, valued over $4,000) for building AI voice into a real product. Open to startups with fewer than 25 employees; direct application.

records.title: PostHog for Startups — $50K in credits for 12 months
records.description: $50,000 in usage credits for a year covering analytics, session replay, feature flags, experiments, and error tracking, plus roughly $12K in partner perks. Open to any startup under 2 years old with less than $5M raised — bootstrapped is fine.

records.title: Mixpanel for Startups — first year free, up to 1B events
records.description: One full year of Mixpanel product analytics free, every feature included. Open to startups incorporated less than 5 years ago that have raised no more than $8M — no VC or accelerator affiliation required.

records.title: Retool for Startups — first year free (up to $60K value)
records.description: 100% off Retool's Team or Business plan for one year, then 25% off year two — for building internal tools and admin panels. Bootstrapped and angel-funded startups explicitly qualify; under $10M raised, founded within the last 10 years.

records.title: Intercom Early Stage — 93% off year one + free Fin AI agent
records.description: Intercom's customer-messaging helpdesk at 93% off in year one (50% year two, 25% year three) plus a year of the Fin AI agent free. Open to new customers with fewer than 15 employees and up to $10M raised — zero funding qualifies.

records.title: Figma Education — free professional design tools for students
records.description: Verified students get free access to Figma Design, FigJam, and Dev Mode with the professional feature set. Sign up with a school email and verify student status.

records.title: Miro Education — free for students for 2 years
records.description: Free Miro workspace for students with unlimited boards, templates, integrations, and monthly AI credits for a team of up to 10. Apply with proof of enrollment.

records.title: Framer for Education — free site builder while you're a student
records.description: Free Framer Basic plan (hosting, design canvas, CMS, monthly AI credits) for enrolled students — a fast way to ship your startup's landing page. Renewable while you remain a student.

records.title: Stripe Atlas — $500 incorporation with $2,500 in Stripe credits
records.description: Full Delaware incorporation (C corp or LLC) including EIN, founder equity, and 83(b) filing for a one-time $500 fee — plus $2,500 in Stripe credits for your first year and access to over $50K in partner discounts. Open to any founder.

records.title: Mercury — free startup banking with a partner perks portal
records.description: Free business checking and savings with no monthly fees, plus a perks portal for account holders with cloud, dev-tool, and SaaS credits (AWS, GitHub, Gusto, and more). Requires an incorporated US business with an EIN.

records.title: Carta Launch — free cap table software under $1M raised
records.description: Carta's cap table platform free for early-stage companies: issue shares, generate SAFEs, model fundraising scenarios, and get 83(b) support. Free while under $1M raised with 25 or fewer stakeholders.

records.title: Ramp for Startups — corporate card with $350K+ in partner perks
records.description: Free corporate card, expense management, and business account with access to over $350K in partner credits and discounts. Self-serve application for incorporated US businesses; standard underwriting applies.

records.title: Cooley GO — free startup legal document generators
records.description: Free attorney-built document generators from law firm Cooley: Delaware incorporation package, YC SAFE financing docs, NDAs, offer letters, and advisor agreements. Open to any founder — no client relationship required.

records.title: Notion for Startups — up to 6 months free with AI
records.description: Up to 6 months of Notion's Business plan with Notion AI free for eligible startups; smaller teams qualify for 1–3 months.

records.title: Google for Startups Cloud Program — cloud credits
records.description: Google Cloud credits and technical support for eligible early-stage startups — credit amounts scale with your stage.

records.title: AWS Activate — up to $5,000 in credits for self-funded startups
records.description: AWS promotional credits for early-stage startups: up to $5,000 for self-funded teams, and up to $200,000 through affiliated accelerators and investors.

records.title: Microsoft for Startups — up to $150,000 in Azure credits
records.description: Up to $150,000 in Azure credits plus access to AI models and developer tools for early-stage startups. No outside funding required to apply.

records.title: GitHub Student Developer Pack — 50+ free dev tools
records.description: Free access to 50+ developer tools and services for verified students — GitHub Pro, cloud credits, IDEs, and more. If you're building anything technical, start here.

records.title: Afore Founder-in-Residence University (FIR U)
records.description: Two-month founder program exclusively for students, dropouts, and recent grads (within 2 years): $20K-$100K+ investment on a YC-style SAFE (terms per team), office space, 1:1 mentorship, and a closing showcase to 200+ VC firms; rolling monthly admission, enrolled students welcome, no dropping out required. Flags: full-time commitment for the 2-month program; must be in San Francisco; housing not provided.
records.ideal_candidate: A technical student or recent grad ready to build an MVP full-time in SF with pre-seed backing.

records.title: SOSV SF / SOSV NY Accelerator (formerly IndieBio)
records.description: Top early-stage deep tech/biotech accelerator (therapeutics, diagnostics, climate, agtech, foodtech, AI/compute): invests roughly $250K for ~8% equity with up to ~$525K total, plus lab space and a ~4-month intensive program; applications accepted year-round on a rolling basis. Flags: open to the public, not student-specific (many founders are grad students/recent PhDs); equity investment, not a grant; full-time in-person commitment required.
records.location: San Francisco, CA and New York, NY
records.ideal_candidate: A graduate student or PhD researcher ready to commercialize a science-based technology full-time.

records.title: Global Student Entrepreneur Awards 2027 (GSEA)
records.description: The premier global competition for students who own and operate a revenue-generating business while in school. Winners advance from local to national to Global Finals for a share of $100,000 in cash prizes plus mentorship and EO network access; no participation cost, travel covered.
records.location: Global - local qualifying competitions in 100+ cities; Global Finals in Cape Town
records.ideal_candidate: Enrolled undergrad or grad students (any school), roughly ages 18-30, who are founder/controlling shareholder of a business operating 6+ months, typically with revenue.

records.title: SXSW EDU Launch Startup Competition 2027
records.description: Live pitch competition for early-stage education/edtech startups at SXSW EDU 2027. Finalists get two complimentary credentials, startup bootcamp access, mentorship, and a live pitch before investors and education leaders. Application fees apply ($60 early / $100 final).
records.ideal_candidate: Founders of early-stage edtech/education startups - open to anyone including student founders from any school (not student-only).

records.title: Thiel Fellowship
records.description: A two-year, $250,000 equity-free grant for young people who want to build new things instead of sitting in a classroom. No equity taken; fellows get access to the Thiel Foundation's network of founders, investors, and scientists.
records.ideal_candidate: Anyone 22 or younger without a university degree who can show meaningful progress toward a concrete vision (company not required). Selected fellows must leave school to accept.

records.title: Emergent Ventures
records.description: Low-overhead grant and fellowship program funding 'zero to one' moonshot ideas that meaningfully improve society; grants commonly range ~$1,000 to $50,000+, non-dilutive. Application is a short form plus a proposal of no more than 1,500 words, with responses typically within weeks.
records.company: Mercatus Center at George Mason University
records.ideal_candidate: Ambitious thinkers and doers age 13+ with an unusual, highly scalable idea - student founders are frequent recipients; AI-related proposals are a current priority.

records.title: 1517 Medici Project Grants
records.description: No-strings-attached cash grants (minimum $1,000) for young people building projects and prototypes in science, tech, math, or the arts. 1517 takes no equity or IP and can later invest further capital if the project becomes a startup.
records.ideal_candidate: High school students, college students, or dropouts obsessively working on a passion project that is not for school credit - driven makers who can't not build it.

records.title: Merge Grant
records.description: $100-$1,000 microgrants with no strings attached - no equity, ownership, or future right to invest - for cash-constrained young builders (hardware, software, research, creative work). Includes ~$800K in partner credits (Stripe Atlas, Supabase, Vercel) and community membership.
records.ideal_candidate: Young builders who can't self-fund and need a small check to clear first blockers; short application plus a relaxed 15-minute interview, ~10 days from application to funding.

records.title: Afore Grants
records.description: $1,000 in non-dilutive, equity-free funding plus paired mentorship from an experienced founder and an investor, weekly office hours and talks, and office space access over a ~12-week exploration period. Application is one question followed by a 10-minute interview.
records.location: Remote, North America (SF office access available)
records.ideal_candidate: High-agency student builders age 21 or younger who want to explore a bold idea before it's VC-fundable.

records.title: Awesome Foundation Micro-grants
records.description: $1,000 no-strings-attached micro-grants awarded monthly by each chapter for 'awesome' projects in arts, technology, community, and more. No equity, no reporting requirements.
records.location: Global - 40+ US city chapters plus thematic chapters
records.ideal_candidate: Anyone (students at any school included) with a novel, delightful, or experimental project - best for creative/community/tech projects needing a small boost rather than startup capital.

records.title: NSF I-Corps Teams (National Program)
records.description: $50,000 non-dilutive grant plus a 7-week entrepreneurial customer-discovery training program for teams exploring commercialization of university lab technologies. Multiple cohorts run year-round; an I-Corps for Quantum+X opportunity opened June 2026.
records.location: US - remote training with some in-person cohort components
records.ideal_candidate: Grad/undergrad student entrepreneurs (as Entrepreneurial Lead) on a team from any US institution with technology connected to university research (typically via NSF lineage or an I-Corps Hub regional course).

records.title: Neo Residency (Startup & Student Tracks)
records.description: 3 months of SF workspace, a 2-week Oregon bootcamp, and 1:1 mentorship. Startup track: $750K uncapped (participation rights up to 5% in next equity round) + $450K+ compute credits. Student track: $40K grant per person + $100K+ compute credits, no equity.
records.ideal_candidate: Explicitly built for high-agency student teams from any school alongside startup founders; extremely selective (12-15 startups, 5-8 student teams per cohort).

records.title: Z Fellows
records.description: A 1-week intensive that gives builders $10,000 (optional - as an investment at a $1B valuation cap, or participate with no money/no equity) plus mentorship from founders of Figma, DoorDash, Netflix, and Ramp. Multiple cohorts per year with lifetime community support.
records.location: Mostly virtual; final day in-person in SF or NYC
records.ideal_candidate: Technical builders of all ages - high schoolers, college students from any school, and dropouts; no company, team, or incorporation required.

records.title: a16z speedrun (next cohort, SR008)
records.description: ~12-week program investing up to $1M per company (typically ~$750K-$1M on SAFE terms disclosed at offer), plus $7M+ in partner credits and a launch platform across talent, GTM, and fundraising. Acceptance rate under 0.4%.
records.ideal_candidate: Ambitious early founders including students and new grads (many past participants under 25); tech/AI/games-adjacent startups from any school or background.

records.title: Antler US Residency (Winter 2026 Cohort)
records.description: Day-zero residency backing founders from inception (US terms historically ~$200K-$250K via SAFE; follow-on up to $30M through Series C). Structured residency for ideation, co-founder matching, and building to an investment decision.
records.location: San Francisco, Austin, or New York City
records.ideal_candidate: Founders from any school/background ready to go full-time (Antler requires leaving school/job commitments) - best for graduating students or those taking leave. No prior company or idea required.

records.title: Greylock Edge
records.description: Bespoke 3-month company-building program for pre-idea, pre-seed, and seed founders with fully flexible financing - from a priced seed round to an uncapped SAFE to no capital at all - plus $500K+ in cloud credits, AI researchers in residence, and hands-on recruiting/customer help.
records.ideal_candidate: Exceptional software founders (AI, infra, cybersecurity, SaaS, consumer, fintech) at day zero - no other prerequisites, so student and new-grad founders from any school can apply.

records.title: Soma Fellows
records.description: Fellowship offering up to $2M in uncapped SAFE funding, plus office space in SF/NY, OpenAI/Anthropic credits, Fortune 500 customer intros, and weekly dinners with founders of Ramp, Cognition, Deel, Kalshi, and 30+ other Soma-seeded unicorns. Potential fast $10M+ follow-on for strong traction.
records.location: San Francisco or New York (office space provided); remote-friendly
records.ideal_candidate: Originally built for student founders and still skews to young builders in college or early 20s from any school; also open to anyone building an early-stage company.

records.title: Dorm Room Fund (Rolling Pre-Seed Funding)
records.description: The original student-run pre-seed venture fund, writing $90K-$250K first checks into companies founded by current students and recent alumni, plus intros to top VC firms and the #DRF4Life founder/investor community. Investment (dilutive), not a grant.
records.ideal_candidate: Student founders (undergrad, MBA, PhD) or recent alumni at any US school raising a first/pre-seed round.

records.title: gBETA Free 7-Week Accelerator
records.description: Free, no-fee, no-equity 7-week accelerator running multiple times per year across US cities: individualized coaching, mentor swarms, pitches to 25+ investors, and $1M+ in vendor perks (IBM, Amazon, HubSpot, Microsoft). ~5 hrs/week, so compatible with coursework.
records.ideal_candidate: Very-early-stage founders (students from any school welcome) located in or near a gBETA market city.

records.title: Halcyon Fellowship (Rolling Eligibility; US Health Accelerator 2026 open)
records.description: Equity-free fellowships for impact-driven, for-profit ventures aligned with UN SDGs: stipends, two DC residencies, monthly virtual programming, and an expert/mentor network. A year-round rolling eligibility form feeds invitations when programs open (currently the US Health Accelerator 2026).
records.ideal_candidate: Founders at MVP stage with users/customers. Requires working full-time on the venture - best for graduating students or those taking leave.

records.title: Future Founders Fellowship - 2027 Cohort
records.description: Free, no-equity, year-long fellowship for entrepreneurs 18-30 with growing (typically revenue-generating) startups: mentoring, EIRs, founders' weekends in Chicago, peer community, and a 3-year Alumni Accelerator afterward. School enrollment is not a factor - students at any school qualify.
records.location: US nationwide; mostly virtual with Chicago retreats
records.ideal_candidate: US residents age 18-30 who are founder/equity-holders in a C-level decision-making role actively growing a startup.
